newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond curve continues to flatten.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond curve continues to flatten.

text.p: The Australian futures curve closed at its flattest level since early January and the spread of 10-year bonds to the U.S. closed at the top of the 75-80 points resistance band on Thursday.
While the local market was softer after Treasuries weakened on Wednesday, the long end proved resilient on the day and managed to hold above support.

The spread to U.S. 10-years closed at 80 points, near the close of 79 points posted earlier this week. Local bond yields have not been this close to U.S. Treasuries since February 1994, and traders expect them to remain well supported into the lead up to next week's December quarter inflation data.
The short end softened in the afternoon to close leaning on support, which saw spreads to other dollar bloc short bonds closed mixed.
The resilience of the long end on the day saw a flattening in the yield curve, with the futures curve moving back under 100 points to close at its flattest level since January 6.

Traders said that if the Australian dollar, which fell to 5-1/2 month lows on Thursday, continued to weaken the short end may underperform as expectations of another easing in official cash rates were wound back.
As a result, the curve could test towards 90 points.
